shots.composition_notes: Single locked-off wide two-shot of a stop-motion kitchen, camera never moves for the full 13s. Woman occupies left third seated at a kitchen island holding a teacup, framed from waist up with generous headroom above her bun; window behind her fills the upper-left background. Man occupies right-of-center, cropped at the waist by the counter/dishwasher, alternating between loading dishes and reaching up to a cabinet; his body stays roughly centered in the right two-thirds. Kitchen counters, stove, and cabinets fill the background on both sides with shallow depth (soft-focus greenery visible through the window). Neither character is ever isolated in their own shot -- both stay in frame simultaneously for the entire scene, so all comedic beats (her deadpan reactions, his frantic dish-loading) play out via blocking/expression within one static composition rather than via cutting or reframing.

End-card graphic: black background with centered title "LOW BATTERY PEOPLE" in yellow serif type, "CREATED BY NIN." beneath in white, and a yellow "NEW EPISODE DAILY" ribbon graphic lower-center. No live-action/animated character content, no camera movement -- purely a static title card.

framing_patterns_notes: The entire sketch is shot as one uninterrupted static wide two-shot with no camera movement, pans, zooms, or cuts between characters -- comedy relies entirely on simultaneous visibility of both performers' reactions in a single frame rather than cutaways or close-ups. An "Episode 31" title card ('COLLATERAL DAMAGE') is burlaid directly over the live scene partway through rather than cutting to a separate title shot, preserving the unbroken take. The only true shot change in the whole clip is the transition from the kitchen scene to the black end-card at the very end.
